Today, February 12th 2025, the Capital Area Food Bank is operating solely in an administrative capacity, and there will be no deliveries or pickups due to the current weather conditions. For partners who have orders scheduled for tomorrow or Friday, we plan to operate under normal conditions. However, if you anticipate that your agency will be closed due to the weather, please reach out to Customer Relations as soon as possible to discuss rescheduling your order at partnersupport@capitalareafoodbank.org or 202-644-9845. We appreciate your cooperation and understanding as we work together to ensure everyone's safety during this weather event. We are actively monitoring the situation and will keep you updated with any changes regarding our operations for the rest of the week. Thank you for your partnership. Stay safe and warm! We hope this message finds you well. Today, February 12th 2025, the Capital Area Food Bank is operating solely in an administrative capacity, and there will be no deliveries or pickups due to the current weather conditions.

For partners who have orders scheduled for tomorrow or Friday, we plan to operate under normal conditions. However, if you anticipate that your agency will be closed due to the weather, please reach out to Customer Relations as soon as possible to discuss rescheduling your order at partnersupport@capitalareafoodbank.org or 202-644-9845.

Additionally, even if your site remains open, we require confirmation that your location has been safely plowed and salted to allow for safe deliveries. If a driver arrives at your site and finds it is not adequately prepared, please be aware that your agency may incur a restocking fee. Our delivery equipment cannot navigate through snow or ice safely, and we prioritize the safety of both our drivers and your staff.

We appreciate your cooperation and understanding as we work together to ensure everyone's safety during this weather event. We are actively monitoring the situation and will keep you updated with any changes regarding our operations for the rest of the week.
Thank you for your partnership. Stay safe and warm!

Please note that we are rescheduling orders, with the earliest openings being mid-week next week. This is due to our delivery and pickup schedules being full before the snow we experienced this week. Please reach out to us to coordinate further!

We are fully aware of the impact that inclement weather can have on our collective efforts, and we remain committed to ensuring the safety of our staff and yours during this time. Thank you for your understanding and support as we navigate this situation together. We are working quickly to get back on schedule.

Thank you for your question. Once you complete the checkout process, your items are put on a sales order and finalized. The emails you receive are due to potential errors in our inventory or the pulling process that may cause changes to your order before delivery.

This can happen for two main reasons. Firstly, if the pulling team finds that the item's quality is not up to our standards for delivery, it may be removed from your order or the quantity decreased. This can occur when partners place orders well in advance and by the time the order is picked, the item may no longer meet our quality standards.
Secondly, if we run out of a certain product, this could be due to periodic inventory errors where the actual count of items doesn't match what's on the menu.
While we strive to minimize these occurrences, we send email notifications to keep partners informed in case such changes are necessary before their order is fulfilled.

Thank you for reaching out about the expiration dates on your product. Unfortunately, we cannot provide specific expiration dates for these items. When a product is labeled as ""assorted,"" it means it is a compilation of dozens of different products under that category that have been donated. These items are sorted by our volunteer teams or donated in bulk.

While our volunteers are instructed not to include expired foods, items that are past their ""best by"" or ""sell by"" dates are considered acceptable for consumption and may still be included. We encourage all partners receiving these donated cases to be aware of this and to use the Food Coding Guide created by our Food Resources team and Nutrition Department. Additionally, we recommend using your knowledge of food safety and your senses (sight, smell, and texture) to determine if the food is in good condition.

I apologize for not being able to provide further guidance on this matter. The nature of donated products, especially assorted bins, makes it difficult to pinpoint a specific expiration date for a mix of different items.

column1: Thank you for submitting this ticket to Customer Service. I have reviewed your reported issues and consulted with my colleagues in our Food Resources and Operations Teams.

Regarding the tortillas, I apologize that they were sent out after their expiration date. I have reported this to the Food Resources Team for further investigation. However, since you received them, I have processed a credit of $45.60 for the tortillas you ordered (which had a discount applied). This credit will be applied to the invoice associated with your order, Invoice #180569.

As for the flavored water, the date on the items indicated ""BB,"" which stands for ""best by."" Many of our donated foods may be past their best by or sell by dates. These dates are intended to inform you of when the item is not at its peak quality, not about food safety. The items are still safe to consume, and we encourage our partners to use their judgment. If there are any signs of concernâ€”such as changes in taste, smell, or packagingâ€”do not distribute the item and please let us know.

column1: Thank you for submitting this ticket to Customer Service. I have reviewed your reported issues and consulted with my colleagues in our Food Resources and Operations Teams.

Regarding the tortillas, I apologize that they were sent out after their expiration date. I have reported this to the Food Resources Team for further investigation. However, since you received them, I have processed a credit of $45.60 for the tortillas you ordered (which had a discount applied). This credit will be applied to the invoice associated with your order, Invoice #180569.

As for the flavored water, the date on the items indicated ""BB,"" which stands for ""best by."" Many of our donated foods may be past their best by or sell by dates. These dates are intended to inform you of when the item is not at its peak quality, not about food safety. The items are still safe to consume, and we encourage our partners to use their judgment. If there are any signs of concernâ€”such as changes in taste, smell, or packagingâ€”do not distribute the item and please let us know.

I hope this message finds you well. Thank you for your valuable feedback regarding our delivery process.  I will connect with our Transportation Team to clarify the issue and explore ways to improve it. Each morning, our Transportation Leadership prints out the day's sales orders, which should include the notes you and your team leave. I will double-check to ensure this process is still in place, as we established a notes section specifically for partners to provide important information for our drivers.  Additionally, I want to mention that there are times when drivers may finish their deliveries earlier than expected, or we may have more drivers available than anticipated. In such cases, drivers are instructed to call you to ask if you would like to receive your order before your scheduled delivery window. If you decline, they should wait until your designated delivery window.  I will reach out to confirm these details and will follow up with you. I understand that the current situation is not ideal and the implications it has on your distribution.

More importantly, it is mandatory for them to call all partners before their deliveries, even if they are within the designated delivery window. This call is to inform you that they are on their way. I hope you are doing well. I wanted to bring this matter to Austin and discuss it with her. I understand the implications of the large orders and the concerns surrounding the removal of produce for the produce hub. When I spoke to Austin, she suggested that the first step should be to have a conversation with the partner to explain the implications of their edits to the order. They need to be mindful that they donâ€™t want to lose their produce items meant for the hub and that they should be aware of the weight of their orders when placing them.
Here are two key points I discussed with Austin:

1. Currently, we do not have a formal limit for orders, so we cannot tell them what a limit would be. Operations and ERP/IT are working on measures to ensure that for large orders, the number of delivery blocks corresponds appropriately. For example, two weeks ago, Capital Christianâ€™s order required five trucks for delivery but only occupied one slot, which is unrealistic. For now, we can only ensure that Operations is aware and prepared for these situations.

2. Austin mentioned that if this situation continues to cause recurring issues and impacts the produce hub's participating sitesâ€”resulting in a loss of produceâ€”we can consider locking their orders for the produce hubs and requesting that they create a separate order. However, this could complicate matters since Operations has asked us to consolidate orders for the same partner to avoid having one sales order versus two. We can explore this locking option as a last resort if recurring issues continue.
I hope this clarifies the situation, and please let me know if you need any assistance in engaging with the partner.

column1: Order Modifications/Quantity Adjustments,"Good morning CAFB team, I hope my email finds you well. The form to make the request is no longer available which is why I am sending you this email. CAFB has given our Food pantry a limit of 16,250 pounds per month but we would be grateful if we could have a very higher produce allocation otherwise our distribution will be in trouble. The first reason is that each week we have over 500 guests at our Food distribution (several times we have already exceeded 600 guests!) and the number is only increasing. We have 4 distributions in a month. 16,250 pounds per month is 8 pallets per month. We cannot feed more than 500 people per week with only 8 pallets per month so we will be forced to reduce our distribution to 1 day per month instead of 4 per month. 8 pallets is the minimum number of pallets of food we use for a single distribution in the month. If you look at our order history, for the past several months we have been doing 2 orders per week, one on Tuesday and one on Wednesday in order to have enough produce for all the families that come. The second reason is that CAFB is our only food supplier. If you maintain the limit of 16,250 pounds per month, the question for us will be: how are we going to get the difference in food that we will no longer have? Having no other suppliers, the only solution will still be to reduce the distribution days. The third reason is that we do not make our choices based on the pound because we have the space in our Gym to store at least 40 pallets against the wall, if they are pallets stored one on top of the other, that makes us more than 80 and we can also store 12 pallets in our Food pantry room so we have plenty of space to store the food. We make our choices taking into account the diversity of food because of the diversity of cultures who come to take the food. I hope that all these explanations will make us find favor in your eyes so that you increase our pound limit. Thank you in advance. The third reason is that we do not make our choices based on the pound because we have the space in our Gym to store at least 40 pallets against the wall, if they are pallets stored one on top of the other, that makes us more than 80 and we can also store 12 pallets in our Food pantry room so we have plenty of space to store the food. We make our choices taking into account the diversity of food because of the diversity of cultures who come to take the food.
I hope that all these explanations will make us find favor in your eyes so that you increase our pound limit.

This year, our Food Procurement Team purchased two truckloads of turkeys, each at a cost of approximately $60 to $70 per case and were available on PartnerLink. These turkeys have been allocated to various orders and are no longer available.

I reached out to my colleagues on the Food Resources Team, who informed me that we often receive donated turkeys. These donations will be provided at no cost now that the shared maintenance fee has been waived for donated items. _However_, *we cannot predict if and when these donations will arrive*. Typically, individuals and organizations tend to donate turkeys closer to Thanksgiving, usually in the week before the holiday or during the holiday week itself.
Please continue to check the menu regularly to see if turkeys are added. If we do receive them, they will be added to the menu and available to partners on a first-come, first-served basis.
We buy Turkey every year from CAFB in bulk you can check your record.
I think our organization should have been given some consideration during the sharing of 2 trucks load of Turkey.
We don't rely on donations we buy our Turkey every year.
We observed that since Elvis left we have been having issues inrespect of our order, this is very unfair.
Our community are expecting thanksgiving Turkey from us only to disappoint them at the end.

I hope this message finds you well. Thank you for reaching out to me again regarding the turkey availability. I completely understand how important this is for your community, especially during the holidays.

I want to clarify that all the turkeys we receive are available on a first come, first served basis for all our partners, just like other items on the menu. I also realize that in previous years, there was a fee associated with our donated turkeys (0.19 cents per pound). However, Iâ€™m pleased to share that this fee has been waived for this fiscal year, so itâ€™s possible you may have paid in the past but you would not have to this time for the donated product.

I genuinely want to ensure that you and your clients receive the support you need this holiday season. I understand how quickly these items can disappear from the menu, and I encourage you to check it daily, as we frequently add new products. Right now, we also have vegetable oil, stuffing mix, corn muffin mix, canned collard greens, and beans that might help supplement your holiday distributions.
Please feel free to check the menu regularly, and if I see any additional turkeys come available, I will reach out to you.
Thank you for your understanding, and know that we are here to support you and your community during this important time.

Thank you for contacting us about food item dates and quality issues. We want to ensure that all the food leaving our warehouse is safe for consumption and properly dated for your knowledge. Some of the items you mentioned are *donated products*. As we increase the donated products on our menu, I want to make sure that all partners are aware that Capital Area Food Bank accepts donations with items past their best by and sell by dates.

The best by date is an indicator of the quality of a product but is not a safety date. The sell by date is for inventory management and tells the store for how long to display the product for sale. The product can still be consumed after this date. It's important to note that many of our donated products will be past these dates, but they are not expired and are still safe for consumption.

We have food coding guides that partners can print and reference during distributions. When available, they can be ordered in English and Spanish from our Nutrition Education Department. The dates on some products may cause concerns for partners and their clients, but we urge you all to differentiate between the different dates on products, use the food coding guide as a reference, and also use your best judgment as well as your food safety knowledge. If you have a product that is not of the right consistency, has an odor, or you believe to be not okay, please let us know and discard the item immediately. As we increase our donations, we may encounter some challenges, but please work with us and continue to provide us with feedback.
Additionally, if you ever have an issue with fresh produce, please include photos of the items so that we can forward them to our Operations and Food Resourcing Departments for their knowledge.

Thank you for contacting us about food item dates and quality issues. We want to ensure that all the food leaving our warehouse is safe for consumption and properly dated for your knowledge. Some of the items you mentioned are *donated products*. As we increase the donated products on our menu, I want to make sure that all partners are aware that Capital Area Food Bank accepts donations with items past their best by and sell by dates.

The best by date is an indicator of the quality of a product but is not a safety date. The sell by date is for inventory management and tells the store for how long to display the product for sale. The product can still be consumed after this date. It's important to note that many of our donated products will be past these dates, but they are not expired and are still safe for consumption.

We have food coding guides that partners can print and reference during distributions. When available, they can be ordered in English and Spanish from our Nutrition Education Department. The dates on some products may cause concerns for partners and their clients, but we urge you all to differentiate between the different dates on products, use the food coding guide as a reference, and also use your best judgment as well as your food safety knowledge. If you have a product that is not of the right consistency, has an odor, or you believe to be not okay, please let us know and discard the item immediately. As we increase our donations, we may encounter some challenges, but please work with us and continue to provide us with feedback.
Additionally, if you ever have an issue with fresh produce, please include photos of the items so that we can forward them to our Operations and Food Resourcing Departments for their knowledge.
We appreciate your partnership with us in this.

Other/Miscellaneous,"Ms. Jackson, Gaithersburg HELP is an all-volunteer organization that has been serving the needy in our local community for 56 years, and we are dedicated to supporting as many families with food each month as we can. In fact, last month HELP served 500 families at our pantry in the Festival Shopping Center. We have only a couple of volunteer drivers who can deliver food, and we must reserve that service for those individuals who live alone or have a partner who also can't drive to the pantry. You had asked for us to deliver food to a family of 9 people. As you must know from your previous food pickups, which total 30 since 2018, we pack according to family size
column2: so a family of 9 would receive at least 8 heavy bags of groceries. We simply can't ask a volunteer, all of whom tend to be over 60 years of age, to pick up and deliver many bags of groceries
column3: and that would not be appropriate when there are able-bodied family members in residence. As an all-volunteer organization, we strive to serve as many families as possible
column4: but we can sustain our operation only if almost all of our families pick up at the pantry. If a client needs to come to the pantry via bus, we offer bus tokens so that transportation to and from the pantry is free. It is not an insult to let someone know that we have limited capabilities for food delivery. It's just a fact. And we would not ask to see proof of disability. We explain our limited delivery ability to any client who asks about delivery. Also, our coordinators always provide information about how to get food from Manna and/or the Gaithersburg Hope Center. Clients can get food from us while also getting food from those other organizations. In that way, we hope clients find they have more money to apply toward rent or utility bills. Our yearly client survey results validate that outcome and that our volunteers treat clients with dignity and promptness. We could serve your family very quickly with food if someone could drive to the pantry or come via bus. Margo On Thu, Nov 14, 2024 at 2:11â€¯PM 'Yvette Jackson' via Info wrote: Dear Capital Area Food Bank Support Team, My name is Yvette Jackson, and I am writing to report an issue I experienced with food assistance delivery from Gaithersburg HELP. On Monday at 9:36 a.m., I called to apply for food assistance delivery, but my request was refused based on the number of people in my household and our ages. Specifically, this refusal has caused significant inconveniences and insult to my family and me, as we urgently need food assistance. Insulting my family by indicating ""With such a large family someone should be able to take the bus here for pick up!"" shows a lack of empathy and compassion. After making a complaint, I received a response at 12:54 p.m. today, indicating that the refusal and statement were correct due to the volunteer nature of the service and their inability to deliver help to a large household. I was directed to seek assistance from other sources such as Manna Food. I believe there might be a misunderstanding or miscommunication regarding our eligibility for this service. Attached to this email, you will find documentation of my disability for your review. column1: Gaithersburg HELP is an all-volunteer organization that has been serving the needy in our local community for 56 years, and we are dedicated to supporting as many families with food each month as we can. In fact, last month HELP served 500 families at our pantry in the Festival Shopping Center. We have only a couple of volunteer drivers who can deliver food, and we must reserve that service for those individuals who live alone or have a partner who also can't drive to the pantry. You had asked for us to deliver food to a family of 9 people. As you must know from your previous food pickups, which total 30 since 2018, we pack according to family size
column2: so a family of 9 would receive at least 8 heavy bags of groceries. We simply can't ask a volunteer, all of whom tend to be over 60 years of age, to pick up and deliver many bags of groceries
column3: and that would not be appropriate when there are able-bodied family members in residence. As an all-volunteer organization, we strive to serve as many families as possible
column4: but we can sustain our operation only if almost all of our families pick up at the pantry. If a client needs to come to the pantry via bus, we offer bus tokens so that transportation to and from the pantry is free.

column1: It is not an insult to let someone know that we have limited capabilities for food delivery. It's just a fact. And we would not ask to see proof of disability. We explain our limited delivery ability to any client who asks about delivery. Also, our coordinators always provide information about how to get food from Manna and/or the Gaithersburg Hope Center. Clients can get food from us while also getting food from those other organizations. In that way, we hope clients find they have more money to apply toward rent or utility bills. Our yearly client survey results validate that outcome and that our volunteers treat clients with dignity and promptness.
We could serve your family very quickly with food if someone could drive to the pantry or come via bus.

Dear Capital Area Food Bank Support Team,
My name is Yvette Jackson, and I am writing to report an issue I experienced with food assistance delivery from Gaithersburg HELP.

On Monday at 9:36 a.m., I called to apply for food assistance delivery, but my request was refused based on the number of people in my household and our ages. Specifically, this refusal has caused significant inconveniences and insult to my family and me, as we urgently need food assistance. Insulting my family by indicating ""With such a large family someone should be able to take the bus here for pick up!"" shows a lack of empathy and compassion. After making a complaint, I received a response at 12:54 p.m. today, indicating that the refusal and statement were correct due to the volunteer nature of the service and their inability to deliver help to a large household. I was directed to seek assistance from other sources such as Manna Food.

I believe there might be a misunderstanding or miscommunication regarding our eligibility for this service. Attached to this email, you will find documentation of my disability for your review. Please note the MetroAccess document on line 16, which indicates that my disability prevents me from independently using the accessible Metrobus and Metrorail system for all trips. I am unable to walk due to L spine disease with a risk of falls, panic attacks, anxiety, and non-tolerance to crowds. At this point, I feel my disability, age, and household circumstances are severely limiting my access to essential help.

I would appreciate your assistance in reviewing this matter and providing any necessary support to ensure that my household can receive the food assistance we need as it appears Gaithersburg Help is not completely meeting the needs of the community. I value your prompt attention to this issue and look forward to your response.

We just received your request for assistance. We will reply as soon as possible.
Thank you for contacting customer support. I am looking into the dates for your previous orders to confirm that they are safe to eat.
As a reference, feel free to use our Food Coding Guide (attached)  as a resource when navigating different dates.
I will follow up with you as soon as I get updates regarding the products you asked about.

I hope you are doing well. I wanted to talk to you about the ticket you submitted. I apologize for the delay. One of my team members brought up your concerns regarding some items you received from us. After discussing your concerns about the salad dressing with my management and the Food Sourcing Team responsible for all the food that comes into the Food Bank, here are some points I wanted to share with you.

Regarding the salad dressing, our Food Resourcing Team does not have a specific recommendation for shelf-stable milk or salad dressing in our Food Coding Guide. We suggest following the USDA's recommendation regarding this product specifically and apologize for not being able to provide further insight. Partners and clients should use their eyes, noses, and, taste buds to determine if a food is spoiled and therefore unsafe to eat. Of course, if a product is showing any signs of spoilage such as rot, mold, foul odor, etc., we will accept a return. I have brought this issue to management's attention, and I agree that our Food Coding Guide needs improvement. I will raise this with our leadership for further review.

In response to your second point, I acknowledge the importance of best-by dates for our partners and their clients. However, our team faces challenges in obtaining these dates for donated products. One challenge arises during packing events when volunteers check and pack donated items into cases labeled as assorted on the menu. These assorted cases contain items from various donors and are packed without specific best-by date information for each individual product. Another challenge occurs when we receive donated products in different case lots-with different dates, making it difficult to provide accurate best-by dates to our partners. We don't know what case lot your order is going to be pulled from until its pulled the day before or two before its delivered or picked up. Although we practice FIFO (first in, first out) inventory management, the dynamic nature of our inventory makes it challenging to predict best-by dates with certainty. As our inventory of donated products increases, we are committed to improving our processes to provide partners with the information they need to make informed decisions. We are continuously seeking ways to improve our processes, and I encourage partners to participate in the upcoming  Partner meetings in July to address any questions or recommendations regarding product dates.
Thank you for bringing these concerns to our attention.

I spoke to the Regional Coordinators and below is the itnel that they had to share about this topic:

_Partners cannot require clients to volunteer in exchange for food. This policy must be clearly communicated between both parties (partner site and volunteer). However, if a volunteer needs food and wishes to continue volunteering, partners have the option to take them on as clients as well. Since you are using Service Insights, the partners will need to create a client profile for the volunteer in the same manner as they do for all clients._
_Volunteers have the same access to food as clients. Therefore, if the partner has zip code or income restrictions, the volunteer must meet the same qualifications as clients do._
Let me know if you need any further questions!

Thank you for reaching out to Customer Relations. I appreciate your inquiry. We offer a variety of fruits and vegetables on our menu throughout the week, but the selection can vary depending on seasonal availability. During the winter months, for example, we typically have fewer options compared to the summer when a wider variety of produce is available.

In recent weeks, the fruits and vegetables available have primarily included potatoes, apples, and carrots. Due to producelimitations placed on agencies, our Food Resources Team is working to bring in more produce items in case lot instead of large bins and full pallets, but this remains an ongoing challenge. Currently, all produce items must be ordered through PartnerLink, as there are no plans to reopen the agency mart for direct pickups.

I have two suggestions to enhance your experience in this situation. First, you can place orders up to 10 days in advance of your scheduled pickup and delivery date. I recommend placing your order as soon as the calendar opens and frequently checking PartnerLink for available produce. You can edit and add to your order until it locks for fulfillment, which is three business days prior to the shipment date. This flexibility allows you to include any additional items you may find during that 10-day window.

Another option is to explore our TEFAP program, a government-subsidized initiative through which participating partners can access additional items to supplement their regular orders. Please note that this program has specific requirements and is managed by the TEFAP team. For more information, you can reach out to Zaynab, the DC TEFAP coordinator: [zkadhem@capitalareafoodbank.org|mailto:zkadhem@capitalareafoodbank.org]

Alanna Food Recall Policy: A food recall, as defined by the FDA, involves removing foods from the market that violate the regulations set by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Foods are recalled for various reasons, primarily due to contamination or failure to disclose essential allergens on the product label. It's important for food suppliers and distributors to stay informed about recalls, as consuming recalled foods may lead to illness or injury. If a product is recalled, the details will be specific to the item reflecting the brand, product name, freeze-by date, and other relevant information pertaining to that specific product. Items that do not match the description provided in the recall notice are not affected and can be safely consumed. In the event of a recall, it is recommended to return the product to the place of purchase or dispose of it to prevent consumption. The Capital Area Food Bank constantly monitors FDA food recall notifications and maintains regular contact with vendors and suppliers. In the event that we are made aware of a recalled inventory item, we will take immediate steps to remove it from all upcoming orders and notify our partners who may have received the item since it was added to our menu. Our Customer Service Team will use various communication channels to promptly inform all partners about the recall and the necessary steps to take with the product. If you have received an item from Capital Area Food Bank that you suspect has caused illness, please contact Customer Relations immediately. Provide your contact information, the date and time of the distribution where the food was distributed to clients, a description of the issue with the product, the item number/name, the date you received the product from our warehouse, and any illness or injury resulting from consuming the item. The Customer Relations Team will handle your complaint seriously and alert the relevant teams at Capital Area Food Bank to address the issue promptly. column1: Thank you for reaching out to Customer Service. You had a great question about our recall process.

For our DDP programs (mobile and community markets), the recall outreach process differs from that of the partnership teams. When a recall is identified, our Food Resources, Analytics, and Operations Teams collaborate with our programs and my team (Customer Relations) to contact the partners who ordered the affected items. It is then the partners' responsibility to reach out to their clients.

For DDP, the process is slightly different. I recommend contacting Jessica Arias, one of our managers on the DDP team, to learn more about how they notify their sites and assist those sites in informing their respective clients.

I apologize for the issues with your two orders. Regarding the Produce Boxes, we have contacted your Regional Coordinators, Grace and Augusta, and they will communicate with Coastalâ€™s Customer Service Team to address the problem with your produce boxes that were not distributable. Augusta has offered to follow up with them and relay any next steps back to you.

As for the peanut butter, thank you for providing photos. We appreciate it. The peanut butter in your order, as well as many of our other donated items, have passed their ""best by"" date. This date indicates when the product will be at its best flavor or quality and is not a safety date. Itâ€™s a quality date that encourages consumers to eat food while it is in its prime state. Food that is past this date is not bad and should not be thrown away. We provide a food coding guide to our partners that explains these dates further. We want to reassure you that the peanut butter is not expired and will not cause any harm to consumers. We offer the Food Coding Guides as a resource and we have them printed and available to order for partners as well to pass out at distributions.

Our system applies grants on a per-line-item basis, which means that only one grant can be applied to each line item. In the case of your order, the line item is $817.00, and the system initially used the last of your FY24 MD Region Moco 1-G grant, which was $75.59.

If this happens, it is because our system applies the grants on a per-line-item basis. If you have a line item that costs less than these amounts in future orders, then you will have no remaining balance.
I hope this clarifies the situation. If you have any more questions, please feel free to ask.

*_Rolled Biscuits: Yield 6-8 biscuits. 1 pkg Jack & the Beanstalk Buttermilk Biscuit Mix, 1/2 cup water, preheat oven to 450 degrees F. Blend biscuit mix and water to a soft dough. Turn dough onto lightly floured surface, knead several times. Pat or roll dough 1/2 inch thick. Cut with 2 inch floured cutter and place on ungreased baking sheet. Bake about 10 minutes. Drop Biscuits: Follow recipe above except do not knead. Drop by spoonful onto ungreased baking sheet. Bake 10-12 minutes._*

*_Do not eat raw batter, dough or mix. Corn Muffins: Yield 6 - 8 muffins depending on size. 1 pkg. Jack & the Beanstalk Cornbread Mix and Corn muffin mix. 1 egg. 1/3 cup milk. Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Grease muffin pan or use paper baking cups. Blend ingredients. Batter will be slightly lumpy. (for maximum crown on muffins let batter rest for 3 or 4 minutes, stir lightly before filling cups.) Fill muffin cups 2/3 full. Bake 15 - 20 minutes or until golden brown._*

We just received your request for assistance. We will reply as soon as possible.

Thank you for your questions about the limited items on the menu. While I don't have a general answer, there are several factors at play. Firstly, at certain times of the year, we have constraints on our receiving calendar, which leads to fewer inventory trucks due to scheduling conflicts. Currently, we are facing this situation as we were closed for Juneteenth, went through our bi-annual inventory last week, and will also be closed for the July 4th observance next week. Additionally, as we prepare for our move back to home building in the Virginia region, there may be a slight shift in the amount of products as we transition inventory from one location to another. This means we have been and will continue to receive fewer trucks than usual and are trying to schedule loads that fit within this restricted schedule.

Moreover, while donations vary, we are actively working to increase the amount of donated food we receive and make it available through our Partner Direct Program and the menu. This issue will be discussed in an upcoming in-person partner meeting in July, giving partners the opportunity to hear from our leadership and our Food Resourcing Team, who are responsible for sourcing all the food on the menu, both donated and purchased.
Let me know if you have any further questions or concerns.

At first sight, we noticed rodent droppings on top of cereal boxes in one of those bins. That bin was not accepted and the delivery driver loaded it back up inside his truck. The other two bins were b *r* ought upstairs to our storage room. To our surprise, a few minutes later, we saw a mouse coming out of one bin and returning inside that bin. We had to act quickly since other food items were stored inside this room. We immediately wrapped both bins, loaded them inside our vehicle and drove to two landfill sites to dispatch the two open bins with donated assorted cereal. Upon dispatching them, our staff saw two mice. This confirmed our fear that more than one mouse had entered inside our building and our storage room through the open bin cereals that we ordered. Of course, the issue was not over and the following Monday, 2/17/25, we caught another mouse. We will continue to closely monitor our storage room and other areas to be certain that the problem has been eradicated. Attached are pictures of what was left behind after we removed the two bins out of the storage room. This experience was very disturbing, and a solution needs to be implemented quickly. This put us behind schedule by four days due to the intervention that we put in place. We also had to throw away our products that the mice had contaminated. CAFB has been such a great partner to us and we are forever grateful for the 'all in' support that you have been providing us to allow us to help our underserved communities. That is why we are sharing this information and our experience to you so this can be further looked at and hopefully avoided. We are in this together to strengthen food security, so we know this kind of issue will be attended to and taken seriously by both parties. I hope youâ€™re doing well today. I was very concerned to hear about the issues youâ€™ve encountered with mice droppings and the presence of mice near the food you received from us. Please know that I am genuinely sorry for this distressing experience, and I want to extend my heartfelt apologies on behalf of Capital Area Food Bank and our Customer Service and Operations Team.

This morning, I forwarded the information you provided in your ticket, along with your photos, to our Director of Operations. She is taking this matter very seriously and has scheduled a meeting with her team to ensure we find a prompt and effective resolution. They will be focusing on maintaining cleanliness and ensuring rodent protection in our facilities, as well as inspecting our warehouse products, particularly those in question, to ensure they are removed if necessary.

I want to support you through this situation. Could you please let me know which specific products you needed to be disposed of due to the potential rodent issue, aside from the bins of cereal? I understand how disruptive this can be to your food distribution efforts, and I truly empathize with the challenges it presents in providing safe and healthy food to the community you serve.
I will also reach out to my supervisor to discuss possible compensation for the inconvenience caused by this situation, as we value your partnership and want to make things right.
Thank you for your understanding, and once again, Iâ€™m truly sorry for the trouble this has caused. We are committed to resolving this matter as quickly as possible.

{color:#172B4D} Thank you so much for your prompt response and for addressing this matter with great regard. We look forward to hearing back from your side the resolution made from your side so this situation can be avoided.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}
{color:#172B4D} When it comes to your questions around damages and pain points that we encounter to intervene quickly here are some of the damages it costs my operations:{color}
{color:#172B4D}We disregard about 50 Rx Boxes that were packed and ready for distribution to our Food as Medicine Program (this is worth $25 each box){color}

{color:#172B4D}We halted our packing operations (2 days' worth) and had caused me loss of 500 Rx Boxes that should have been packed last week. Instead, we used the time to do a deep cleaning to ensure all our 800 Rx Boxes are safe.{color}

{color:#172B4D}We also use two additional days of work to contain and capture the three mice and safely throw the 2 bins of assorted cereals out of our building premises (into a landfill). (Note: I personally set aside my own list of tasks to help my team do this work for two days and also recruit four people to assist us with this problem){color}{color:#172B4D}{color}

{color:#172B4D} I hope this helps you and your organization understand how this type of matters can cause a small organization like ours not only inconvenience/stress but lost of products/investment/productivity for some of our programs outside our Food Pantry operations.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}

Please know that I am genuinely sorry for this distressing experience, and I want to extend my heartfelt apologies on behalf of Capital Area Food Bank and our Customer Service and Operations Team.

This morning, I forwarded the information you provided in your ticket, along with your photos, to our Director of Operations. She is taking this matter very seriously and has scheduled a meeting with her team to ensure we find a prompt and effective resolution. They will be focusing on maintaining cleanliness and ensuring rodent protection in our facilities, as well as inspecting our warehouse products, particularly those in question, to ensure they are removed if necessary.

I want to support you through this situation. Could you please let me know which specific products you needed to be disposed of due to the potential rodent issue, aside from the bins of cereal? I understand how disruptive this can be to your food distribution efforts, and I truly empathize with the challenges it presents in providing safe and healthy food to the community you serve.
I will also reach out to my supervisor to discuss possible compensation for the inconvenience caused by this situation, as we value your partnership and want to make things right.

column3: Thank you for your inquiry on our Hours of Operations Feature on PartnerLink. We encouraged all partners to attend one of the four trainings that we hosted between August and September to ensure that everyone was well-equipped to utilize this feature effectively. This feature is crucial for maintaining accurate information about your agency's operating hours, which in turn updates our [Get Help Map|https://www.capitalareafoodbank.org/find-food-assistance/] on the website. The Get Help Map is a tool that clients use to locate nearby CAFB Partners, so it's essential to have the correct hours displayed. If you were unable to attend the trainings, don't worry. There are alternative options available, such as accessing the resource on PartnerLink under the Partner Resources tab, or signing up for [Customer Relations Office Hours|https://capitalareafoodbank.zoom.us/zbook/partner-support/customer-relations-office-hours] held every Wednesday from 10am-11am. Please note that due to the nature of the training, there are no recordings or slides available, as it involved a live demo and Q&A session. While partners are not being reprimanded for not attending a training, it's important to highlight that starting *October 1st*, partners who have not updated or confirmed their hours will see a banner prompting them to do so before placing an order. You will need to take this action to proceed with making an order. If your hours have not changed, simply verify them by accessing the Agency Overview section after clicking your agency name on PartnerLink. If changes are necessary, please update them accordingly. For further assistance, please contact us at [partnersupport@capitalareafoodbank.org|mailto:partnersupport@capitalareafoodbank.org]. ","09/25/2024 08:16

Additionally, please keep in mind that depending on the amount of snow, there may be impacts on the days following the snowfall. If we do have a closure, we will do our best to accommodate our partners' schedules while ensuring that orders are not affected the following day.

column1: To provide some context, there are two main reasons why drivers may not take pallets when dropping off food during a delivery. Firstly, they may have food for an immediate order or need to pick up food from another site for the warehouse, which means they cannot have food and pallets on the truck at the same time due to food safety (Pallets are often leftoutside- on the ground, possibly in the rain, and are often dirty) and consideration for our partners. Secondly, our drivers may be on tight schedules and do not have the time for a pallet pickup due to their busy delivery schedules, especially during the busy season.
There is no reason why a driver could not explain this to you at the time, and I will ensure that this information is communicated to them. I apologize for your experience.

column1: To give you some background, partners have been charged delivery fees for orders that include a mix of TEFAP products and other donated or purchased items for some time. As stated in our SMART Shopping Policy, orders that contain only TEFAP products do not incur a delivery fee. However, orders that mix TEFAP with purchased or donated products do have a delivery fee associated with them.

I do not have the ability to remove delivery fees from all orders, as these fees are automatically added when partners place their orders. I believe we will need to submit an ERP ticket to stop this charge permanently, as it is an automated process.

To clarify what the ticket would entail: Are we asking for no delivery fees to be applied to any orders containing any TEFAP items for al regions? Additionally, will we need to issue refunds for past orders that were charged delivery fees due to the mix of TEFAP and other products? I anticipate that partners will inquire about previous orders that included these fees as we proceed with this change and it also may be a good idea to plan for a formal communication to TEFAP partners since this is a change in poliy that we have previously stated to them.

Is there a deadline for when this needs to be implemented? I understand that it should be done as soon as possible, but any changes/refunds to delivery fees are always approved by Austin, who is currently out until January 9th.
Thank you for bringing this matter back to our attention again, hope to resolve this as soon as possible!

{color:#172B4D} We also distribute canned goods to those who have a place to cook ( about 6-15) a week.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}

Granted none of this is considered healthy but it is convenient and ready to eat.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}
{color:#172B4D} We also distribute canned goods to those who have a place to cook ( about 6-15) a week.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}
{color:#172B4D} Let me know if you have any questions or need anything else.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}

We appreciate the wonderful service you provide to your community and your partnership with CAFB for the last 15 years. Different programs within CAFB have different rules and regulations. TEFAP falls under the rules and regulations of MD DHS, collection of SDI forms is one of the requirements set forth by them not by myself or by CAFB.

I completely understand that the work that you and all your volunteers do is hard and exhausting work. We also understand that not everyone is able to, qualifies for, or feels comfortable completing the SDI form. This is why we do always recommend there be non TEFAP food set aside for those do not qualify or are unable to complete the SDI form.

My goal is not to suspend New Hope and Life Church of God, it is to work with you and each partner to ensure there is compliance with regulations set forth by MD DHS, to work together when other problems arise, and to get to know each partner to the best of my ability so that I can continue to advocate for change at the state level.

Regarding the monthly inventory report for the month of August, like covered in the civil rights training, regardless of whether food was distributed a report must still be submitted. In the case of no distribution, you would just need to put 0 under the household and individuals served, note any inventory you have at the time, sign and submit.
I can also look at your sales order record and send you the food ordered around that time frame which may help in the completion of the report.

column1: {color:#172B4D} I am happy to arrange the Bailey's site visit.{color}
We just received your request for assistance. We will reply as soon as possible.

column3: {color:#172B4D}Under normal circumstances, yes. However, while speaking with Charity during the training and relaying that I would like to separate the locations, she told me in stead of selecting my own credentials through the link, CAFB would create them for me using my email address for all but a different password for each. Because of this special circumstance, she said that I would not have received the usual email. I would receive an email detailing all locations and passwords.{color}

{color:#172B4D}Okay I see, my apologies! Currently, we have New Hope Housing Kennedy Shelter on Richmond Highway in our records as your approved address. Our partner support team will be happy to get you the login in to that account. If you would like to add a different location, I will need to conduct a site visit to ensure food safety and we will need to have a larger conversation around how the food will be distributed between the two sites. I believe when we spoke on the phone previously, we agreed you would begin ordering again for the Kennedy Shelter to see the types of food we have available. I understood then from there we would see if it made sense to add another location or not based on the different needs. Just a reminder, CAFB food can only be delivered to and stored at the Kennedy Shelter address.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}

column1: {color:#172B4D} Please let me know if that helps.{color}{color:#172B4D}{color}

column1: We appreciate your patience as we look into this issue. Can you please confirm if this was a TEFAP product or not?
Yes, the catfish was a TEFAP product.
Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church{color:#575757}{color}","08/16/2024 01:49

We contacted the TEFAP Team and learned that we anticipate receiving a shipment of catfish between October 16th and 31st. Currently, we do not have a waitlist or a reminder system linked to our inventory to alert partners when items are back in stock. This is feedback we have received from partners and have conveyed to our Food Resourcing and Inventory Teams for consideration.

If you wish to check back during that time and do not see the catfish available, we would be happy to reach out to the TEFAP team to confirm if the shipment is still expected during that period. It seems that in your original order, the product went out of stock. Our inventory is live and operates on a first-come, first-served basis as you know. At times, items may be taken by the time you start the checkout process, resulting in an error message prompting you to update your item quantities based on what's available.

Additionally, there may be different lots of items with varying expiration dates. Consequently, you may have two lots of the same product arriving at different times, with one having a later expiration date than the other. Depending on the date of your order, the item may have gone out of stock for the specific case lot you selected, even though there are still some available on the menu. This occurs due to the date you chose for your order.
We acknowledge that our inventory system is complex and are striving to make it more user-friendly and accessible for partners to obtain information from the website.

I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to give you an update on this issue. I have submitted a help ticket for our Accounting/Finance team so they can intervene and create a credit for your agency for the flour. Customer Service is unable to complete this task, so once I hear back from Accounting, I will be able to confirm that the credit has been created and applied to your agency's account.
Thank you very much for your help.

I just received word from our Finance Team that they have processed a cash refund of $49 to your original form of payment for the cost of the affected flour. Please allow some time for this refund to reach your account. We apologize for the delay in taking this action and for the inconvenience this situation has caused.

I hope you are doing well. I reached out to Food Resources and Operations about this, and I will process a credit from the agency when an invoice is generated for the sales order. I will circle back tomorrow, and hopefully, an invoice will be generated so I can credit them back for this item.
Thank you for bringing this to our attention.

*Subject:* New PartnerLink Feature- only 2 more training sessions left!{color}

We are excited to announce that the new PartnerLink feature is now live! This feature will allow partners to update their hours of operations for their distributions. This new feature is very exciting because it means that you will be able to update your records whenever necessary. This ensures that we have the most up-to-date information in our internal systems and for clients to utilize. As a reminder, once approved, the information we gather from your updates will be linked to the information provided in our online tool that clients can use to locate food assistance: [Get Help Map|https://www.capitalareafoodbank.org/find-food-assistance/].

To ensure that all partners understand how to utilize this function, we planned to host two trainings, two of which have already occurred and  *+two+* more in the month of September. These sessions are designed to demonstrate how to use this feature and also provide an opportunity to talk to our team about PartnerLink and provide feedback. Please note that this training is  *+mandatory+*. You can use the links below to register your agency. We only require one representative per agency to attend, but we welcome and encourage all shoppers who have access to PartnerLink to join. We recommend that this person work closely with the food program and has a deep understanding of operations. While the training will be recorded and slides will be shared,  *all partners are expected to attend the live training to fulfill the requirement*. If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Customer Relations.

Please [click here|https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=4eNCVd-_qki8SMWEhD1eIsYv8jPOqcdPqqy5Ip3OhsZUN1ZKWjFLWk5EV1NHOUFSSjFLUUtaQ1E3OS4u] to register. Upon selecting a training date and completing the form, you will receive the corresponding Zoom link via email.

We are also excited to announce that the Customer Relations team will be hosting office hours every Wednesday in August & September from 10 am to 11 am starting August 14th. If you have any questions or support needs related to the new PartnerLink feature, this time is available to you.

Additionally, this opportunity will allow partners to interact with the Customer Relations Team, ask questions, and receive additional support regarding PartnerLink, menu items, new website features, and more. Please come prepared with questions and examples of issues that you may be experiencing with PartnerLink. Sharing your experiences is valuable, as it could help others facing similar issues. If you have specific recurring issues unique to your organization, we may need to take down your information and set up a one-on-one meeting to address them thoroughly and ensure the office hours are productive for all partners. Please note that if there are no attendees in the first 15 minutes of the office hours, we will cancel that week's session.
To register for Customer Relations office hours, please click [here|https://capitalareafoodbank.zoom.us/zbook/partner-support/customer-relations-office-hours].
We appreciate your ongoing partnership, collaboration, and look forward to seeing you at one of our training sessions or during our office hours.
